violation_type.title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Set appropriate behavior expectations (26 TAC §744.1203(6))
violation_type.short_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Set appropriate behavior expectations
violation_type.typical_finding: A caregiver did not have classroom control. The children were observed running and not listening to the instructions given by the caregiver, causing the caregiver to have to use higher than normal voice tones to gain the attention of the children.

finding_variants.text: A caregiver did not have classroom control. The children were observed running and not listening to the instructions given by the caregiver, causing the caregiver to have to use higher than normal voice tones to gain the attention of the children.
Based on the information obtained it was determined that the operation was not maintaining control of the children in care.
A caregiver was observed sitting on a bench using his phone to sketch a drawing on paper while children were playing on the playground.
Caregiver did not set appropriate expectations.

Deficiency re-cited. Children were observed running in the cafeteria multiple times. One child was observed slapping another child n the face from across the table. One child was observed hitting another child in the face with his backpack. One child was observed under a cafeteria table. One child was observed carrying an unraveled paper clip; when staff told child to throw it away, the child walked back to his table and put it in his pocket.
I observed a caregiver with the operation under all sports and enrichment on his cell phone outdoor with children.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Set appropriate behavior expectations: Inspector observed children whistling/hooting loudly, running, not listening to staff or sitting down, and no transition activity was provided for approximately 27 minutes. Inspector also observed one child playing on cell phone and throwing paper balls at each other. Inspector did observe staff using a whistle to try and get children to sit down and listen however no appropriate behavior boundaries were given.
